problem: For Poisson-binomial mass functions with variance V ≥ 1, prove that the product of variance and normalized Turán deficit at the first-descent index satisfies V·δD ≥ 1/4.
debate: The paper enters the literature on Turán inequalities and log-concavity for probability mass functions, addressing limitations of existing bounds that scale with n or individual success probabilities.
gap: Existing lower bounds on Turán inequalities either scale with n or depend on success probabilities and degenerate when probabilities near 0 or 1; the gap is whether variance alone controls the decay rate.
contribution: The paper proves V·δD ≥ 1/4, establishes that this constant is optimal to within a factor of 4/3 (showing κ⋆ ≤ 1/3), and derives explicit geometric decay past the mode.
note: Advance—the result is clear and rigorous, but the gap from 1/4 to the true optimum of at most 1/3 means you must justify why readers should care about the loose bound.
